messages:
maya: heads-up — seeing a spike in TLS handshake failures between eu-west proxies and user-service after last RBAC change to keystore roles. 502s on proxy with TLS alert handshake_failure. sample log: `tls_handshake: alert(40) client->server, verify failed: unwrap denied`

sam: when was the RBAC change deployed?

deploy-bot: change applied 2026-03-21T06:12:03Z by ci/cd#3421 — role keystore-read -> keystore-read-v2 (narrower scope)

anita: that was the scoped keystore split. did we update proxy IAM to use new role?

maya: not intentionally. I think callers still reference old role ARN. getting repeated KMS unwrap DENIED in the audit stream. quick paste of inner log: ```2026-03-21T06:12:12Z eu-west proxy requestid=aa11 tls: unwrap result=DENIED key=svc/user-service/kek error="permission denied"```

leo: I pulled audit logs for last 30m — about 118 DENIED unwraps from proxy instances eu-west-1b. link: https://internal-gists/redwood/abcd1234 (redacted)

security-oncall: marking as P1 for now. action plan: 1) pause rollout / rollback RBAC change in eu-west 2) collect full KMS unwrap audit lines + proxy TLS traces 3) check certchain and SNI mappings 4) postmortem if regression.

ops-bot: suggested immediate mitigation: add a temporary service-account binding that maps old role to new role for proxy pods (short TTL). Will create a PR. :gear:

sam: can we verify whether this is strictly RBAC -> unwrap DENIED or whether proxy is also sending wrong client cert (SNI mismatch)? check for `client_hello.sni` mismatches in traces.

anita: adding note — keystore split also changed key alias prefixes. proxies that fallback to alias resolution may now send an alias that KMS denies. So both RBAC and alias drift possible.

maya: running audit query now: `SELECT timestamp, principal, action, status, key FROM kms_audit WHERE action='Decrypt' AND status='DENIED' AND region='eu-west-1' LIMIT 200` — returns proxy principal x 118 with key prefixes `svc/user-service/*` and reason `role: not authorized`.

leo: corroborating network side: client_hello for ~30% of failed sessions shows SNI `user-service.legacy.prod` while cert presented expects `user-service.internal`. Could be old sidecars.

security-oncall: ok, prioritized sequence: 1) rollback keystore role change in eu-west to restore unwraps 2) rotate proxy sidecar rollout to ensure new alias prefix and SNI 3) add an audit alert rule: when KMS unwrap DENIED > 20/min raise pager 4) update pre-deploy test to exercise KMS unwrap with new role mapping.

maya: rolling back now in eu-west canary (k8s job applied). watching unwrap success counters.

deploy-bot: rollback job completed 2026-03-21T06:20:02Z — rollout status: canary succeeded on 3/3 pods.

sam: metrics: unwrap DENIED dropped from 118 -> 4 in last 3m. TLS handshake failures reduced accordingly.

security-oncall: good containment. follow-ups assigned: - anita: add alias resolution test to keystore CI - leo: add SNI check to proxy e2e - maya/sam: create postmortem draft and include rollout gating change

ops-bot: created temporary mapping PR #789 to keep old role mapping for 1h while we fix callers.

maya: thanks all. we should also add a line to the runbook: "whenever keystore RBAC scope tightens, run KMS unwrap smoke on a canary proxy before global rollout" :memo:

security-oncall: noted. closing incident if metrics remain stable for 30m. please ping here when done. :white_check_mark:
